title: A Multi‐Scale Analysis of Nitrate Concentration‐Discharge Relationships in a Small Agricultural Watershed
content:
Abstract

Applying a nested watershed framework to concentration-discharge (cQ) relationships provides insight into how solute transport dynamics vary across spatial and temporal scales. We examined nitrate-N cQ relationships at two nested sites within a small agricultural watershed using 3 years of 30-min data. Composite (all data) and event-scale responses were evaluated using multiple metrics, including the flushing index (FI), hysteresis index (HI), cQ slope (b) and CV C /CV Q . Random forest models were used to identify hydrologic controls on inter-event variability and spatial consistency in cQ behavior. Composite relationships showed nitrate-N enrichment, while event-scale patterns were dominated by dilution, a discrepancy due in part to nitrate-N enrichment during storm recession. Antecedent moisture primarily governed inter-event variability in FI and b, while storm magnitude more strongly regulated HI. Rising limb (FI) responses were generally more consistent across sites, while whole-event (b) and hysteresis (HI) behavior exhibited greater divergence, particularly under dry antecedent conditions. Spatial consistency increased when hydrologic connectivity was high, either due to wet antecedent conditions or high-intensity storms that rapidly activated flow networks. These findings underscore the need for multi-scale, event-based monitoring to improve water quality prediction.
